title: Geo fleet run-rate and per-token burn projection
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet walks through a month-by-month run-rate rollforward (Nov 2025 -> Oct 2026) for GPU capacity across NA/EU/APAC and converts expected GPU-hour burn into $/1M tokens under multiple operating assumptions. Goal is to provide a single-page reference for finance, infra planning, and product tradeoffs (reserved vs spot, utilization targets, routing policies).

High-level approach and assumptions (single-line items):
- Convert provisioned GPU-hours * effective utilization * tokens_per_gpu_hour -> tokens served.
- Effective $/GPU-hour = instance-hour cost + infra overhead + amortized tooling/SRE + expected preemption/failed-job uplift.
- Token yield per GPU-hour is workload-dependent; we use three model classes (small chat, medium multi-turn, large completion) with conservative and optimistic yield bands.
- We show baseline (current mix), growth (20% monthly request growth for 6 months then 10% thereafter), and stress spike (3x baseline sustained for 2 weeks) scenarios.

Inputs (key knobs):
- Regions: NA, EU, APAC
- Instance classes & raw cloud rate ($/GPU-hour): A100-80GB (NA $3.10, EU $3.25, APAC $3.65), H100-80GB (NA $6.40, EU $6.85, APAC $7.10), A10G (NA $0.95, EU $1.05, APAC $1.20)
- Reserved discount assumed vs on-demand: 30% for committed, spot multiplier 0.45 of on-demand with 12% effective eviction overhead (i.e. need +12% buffer).
- Infra overhead (load balancers, networking, control plane, storage amortization): $0.18/GPU-hour (globally uniform baseline).
- SRE/tooling/monitoring & support allocation: $0.09/GPU-hour (amortized across fleet).
- Ops uplift for failure/inefficiency (batch padding, cold starts): 6% of GPU-hours as capacity buffer.
- Tokens per GPU-hour (effective delivered tokens):
  * Small chat (gpt-small-ish flows, avg seq 128, short decode): 4.2M tokens/GPU-hour (conservative 3.4M, optimistic 5.1M)
  * Medium multi-turn (avg seq 512, modest decoding): 1.25M tokens/GPU-hour (band 1.0M - 1.6M)
  * Large completion (long outputs, seq 2048, heavy decode): 0.28M tokens/GPU-hour (band 0.22M - 0.37M)

Derived unit economics (method):
1) Compute "all-in $/GPU-hour" = cloud_rate * instance_factor + infra_overhead + SRE_allocation + eviction_buffer_cost + committed/spot mix effect.
2) $/1M tokens = (all-in $/GPU-hour) / (tokens_per_GPU_hour / 1,000,000)

Example calculation (NA, baseline mix using A100 reserved heavy with some burst to spot):
- Raw cloud rate (A100, NA, reserved effective): $3.10 * (1 - 0.30) = $2.17
- Eviction/spot mix: 12% extra buffer cost applied to spot portion; baseline mix assumed 85% reserved, 10% spot, 5% burst-on-demand -> marginal effect +$0.06/GPU-hour
- Infra + SRE = $0.18 + $0.09 = $0.27
- All-in = $2.17 + $0.06 + $0.27 = $2.50/GPU-hour
- Tokens per GPU-hour (medium multi-turn) = 1.25M -> $/1M tokens = $2.50 / 1.25 = $2.00 per 1M tokens

Regional quick-scan (baseline mix, medium model):
- NA: all-in approx $2.50/GPU-hr -> $/1M tokens = $2.00
- EU: base rate slightly higher (reserved ~ $2.28) -> all-in $2.61 -> $/1M tokens = $2.09
- APAC: higher cloud base (reserved ~ $2.56) -> all-in $2.89 -> $/1M tokens = $2.31

Sensitivity matrix (medium model):
- Utilization uplift from 60% -> 80% (same provisioned fleet but higher effective tokens/GPU-hour due to batch/packing improvements) reduces $/1M tokens by ~18-25% depending on region.
- Moving 20% of workload to an A10G-optimized path (cheaper instances for short tokens) reduces blended $/1M by ~12% but requires engineering to build model-variant pipelines.

Run-rate rollforward (month buckets):
- Nov-25 (current): provisioned 2,200 GPU devices across NA/EU/APAC (mix: 55% A100, 30% A10G, 15% H100), fleet utilization measured ~62% (workload mix: 48% medium, 38% small chat, 14% large completion).
- Dec-25 -> Mar-26: steady growth +10% provisioned/month to chase 70% target utilization; mix shifts +15% A10G to offload small chat.
- Apr-26 -> Jun-26: product launch increases demand; provisioned +30% in April then +10% in May/June. Implement canary region expansion in APAC (add 200 GPUs in APAC, H100 prioritized for high-compute customers).
- Jul-26 -> Oct-26: flatten provisioning; focus on reserved purchases to convert spot usage; target fleet utilization 72-78% across regions.

Runway and burn analysis (conservative baseline):
- Monthly GPU-hour burn (Nov-25 baseline): provisioned-hours/month ~ 2,200 devices * 24 * 30 * utilization 0.62 = ~985,000 GPU-hours/month.
- At $2.50/GPU-hour blended -> monthly spend ~$2.46M -> tokens served/month (medium mix weighted average) ~ (985k * 1.25M tokens/GPU-hr) = 1.23e12 tokens -> $/1M tokens ~ $2.00 -> monthly $/month = 1,230,000 * $2.00 = ~$2.46M (consistency check).
- With planned capacity adds to reach 3,400 devices by May-26 and improving tokens/GPU-hour via batching by +15%, $/1M tokens drops to ~$1.60 in NA baseline case.

Stress case (2-week 3x spike):
- Assume burst policy routes traffic to on-demand H100 and additional rented spot in region; incremental all-in marginal cost jumps to $9-$12/GPU-hour depending on region and instance.
- Effective $/1M tokens for medium model during spike could rise to $7-$10 per 1M tokens depending on instance mix; critical to have fallback model routing and throttle plans to avoid extreme unit cost.

Open questions / action items (next 30 days):
- Confirm reserved contract cadence and renewal windows per region (Ethan to sync with procurement).
- Validate tokens_per_gpu_hour numbers against recent perf bench (Marisol to run quick A/B: medium model, seq 512, batch 16 across A100/H100).
- Add a scenario that models prefix/KV cache effectiveness for chat-heavy workloads (likely 20-35% token savings).
- Engineering: estimate implementation cost and timeline to route short chat to A10G-optimized path (approx 8-10 sprints).
- Finance: map planned reserved buys to cash flow windows and surface for Dec board pack.

Notes and heuristics for PRDs / SRE runbooks:
- Anything above $6/1M tokens for medium workloads should trigger auto-fallback rules (reduce non-critical background generation, degrade sampling temp, or switch to cheaper model).
- Target blended $/1M tokens thresholds: Long-term strategic <= $1.50, Commercial baseline $1.75-2.25, Spike tolerated up to $8 (with explicit approvals).

Appendix: quick reference numbers (baseline bands)
- Token yield bands (tokens/GPU-hr): small 3.4M-5.1M, medium 1.0M-1.6M, large 0.22M-0.37M.
- Representative all-in $/GPU-hour by region (baseline reserved-heavy): NA $2.35-2.75, EU $2.48-2.95, APAC $2.75-3.25.
- Blended $/1M tokens (baseline, mixed models): NA $1.70-2.40, EU $1.85-2.60, APAC $2.00-2.90.

This is a working sheet — numbers intentionally rounded for readability. Please flag any metric that should be promoted to the canonical forecasting workbook (INFRA-FCAST-2026) and I will push a cleaned copy.

Action owner list (owners and quick tasks):
- Priya Nair: coordinate reserved purchase calendar and update committed vs spot mix assumptions.
- Ethan Wu: procurement sync and contract terms confirmation.
- Marisol Vega: perf runs to validate tokens/GPU-hour.
- Daniel Petrov: add a simple Monte Carlo run in the canonical workbook to show probability of hitting $/1M token thresholds under demand uncertainty.

End of sheet.
